You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case `testNotEquals` is simple: it creates two `ZipArchiveEntry` instances with different names ("foo" and "bar") and asserts that they are not equal. The `equals` method of `ZipArchiveEntry` is implemented based on the name field — if names differ, the entries are considered not equal. The `equals` method also handles null values and class mismatches properly. Thus, the test behaves as expected.

The current bug report references corrupted output in zip files when created with many entries and switching from JDK zip classes to commons compress. While the current failure might appear unrelated at first (an equality test), it indirectly concerns correctness in handling zip entries - equality and proper management of entry fields are fundamental to correctly generating zip indexes and avoiding duplicates or collisions.

Inspection of the constructor and methods related to extra fields (which often store additional metadata in zip entries) reveals that `ZipArchiveEntry` uses a map (`extraFields`) to hold extra fields parsed from raw extra bytes. The `setExtraFields` method resets the map and repopulates it followed by a call to `setExtra()`, which merges these fields into a raw byte array set on the underlying entry.

The corruption issue from the bug report might arise from improper handling or merging of these extra fields when many entries are present, leading to corrupted index entries in the archive. The `equals` method only compares the name but does not consider extra fields or other metadata, which might cause subtle bugs if code elsewhere expects entries with different extras to differ or be handled differently.

Hence, the fault likely lies in the handling of extra fields and their merging in `setExtra()` or in the way entries are compared or hashed to build the zip file index, leading to index corruption under high entry counts and similar names.

Next, investigation should focus on methods managing the extra fields and entry metadata, such as `setExtraFields`, `getExtraFields`, `setExtra`, and possibly any methods that compute entry hashes or write entries to the archive. It may also be relevant to check how the entries are used during zip creation to ensure uniqueness and integrity.

Suggested methods for further inspection:  
- `ZipArchiveEntry.setExtraFields(ZipExtraField[])`  
- `ZipArchiveEntry.setExtra()`  
- any method involved in writing the index entries (not present here, may require fetching)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
